note: Ours, read by make-events.js (docs/notes/events.md). evStage = evStageBase + r, stage = stageBase + n (server/event_ids.json, append-only). serve: census ids (the April 2019 pilot, Events Part 1) and types (GEM, Part 2) that are built, the rest is notSelected (an old onlyCensusIds list still works; no serve and no list builds every record). reasonText: the catalogue text of every reason a record or quest is not built. labelPhrases: the reconstruction notes of the event quest records -> label id; reconstructedWhy: the text of every label (shown in the Event Catalog, declared in the Notices). eventType: the value served when the donor value is not in servedEventTypes (3 = plain quest list; never 2 = raid mode with Raid Boards). boardEventType (1 = board mode with the Event Boards button, Part 3): served only on an entry with a board set handed out (KHUX_EVENT_BOARDS, make-events.js); without one a donor 1 is served as eventType. catalogEvStage: the Event Catalog banner (evStageBase + 0, never a record: records are numbered from 1), holding catalogStage (the Training Grounds of the Special Catalog), Details -> catalogUrl.
avatarCatalogNote: Avatar Board Catalog banner (Events Part 7 Task 5b, user 15-11): an evStage in the Special tab (avatarCatalogCategory 1) holding catalogStage, Details -> avatarCatalogUrl; its number is the event_ids.json rows number of avatarCatalogKey (append-only, made by make-events.js when the avatar board records are read). Picture: user 15-11: own gold design in the catalogue family (recon/tools/make_special_banners.py avatar_option, composed of original board cards and the Avatar Coin), written by recon/tools/make_avatar_catalog_banner.py to server/game_data/event_img/<id>.png after the regen; after a change bump imgVersion.

hscNote: Events Part 8 Task 6 (make-events.js hscPrepare / hscRows, spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-ranked-rewards-design.md): records of type hsc.type are High Score Challenges. Their evStage rows get eventCategory hsc.eventCategory (4: the tap opens the High Score mode) and rankingId / scoreMedalListId / scoreStartReward / scoreEndReward; master rows ranking (category hsc.rankingCategory, 6 as the donor HSC rows), rankingReward, evScoreReward, evMedalList. Ids from the record's evStage number r (event_ids.json rows): rankingId rankingBase + r, evMedalList listId medalListBase + r, row ids <table base> + r * perRecord + i. A record without score thresholds is not served (hscNoThresholds).
payableNote: Events Part 4 Task 4 (make-events.js remapItems). payableTypes: the reward types of an objective or a first-clear item that server.js grantItem pays (2 Jewels, 3 medal, 4 munny, 5 material, 7 title, 11 Lux, 13 keyblade, 14 Avatar Coin, 15 Event Coins, 16 Raid Coin, 20 avatar part, 26 Skip Ticket, 28 Skip Ticket+, 33 Spirit part, 40 Platinum Ticket, 41 Draw Ticket, 42 Draw Points); payableDropTypes: the types of an original drop or chest row (3 medal, 5 material, 8 and 9 chest contents the client pays, as in our story reward rows, 15 Event Coins). boosterType 34: a Booster. Built (game_data/boosters.json, Part 6): kept as a type-34 reward with its emblem id, paid by boosters.js (label boosterEffect); not built: not paid here (label boosterLater, player.pendingBoosters; a quest whose only rewards are such Boosters: boosterOnly). Any other type: the quest is not served (rewardTypeUnknown) and the type never reaches a row of the client.
rewardTypeAliasesNote: Events Part 5 Task 3 (make-events.js aliasRewardTypes): reward types of the original rows that the server pays as another type. 18 (an avatar set, e.g. Organization XIII Coat 331 / 332) and 19 (a style avatar part, e.g. Marluxia Style 40083 / 41083) are avatarParts rows: served as 20 (avatar part), the type the client shows in an objective list and grantItem adds once to player.avatarParts (the Special quests serve their sets and styles the same way, the ♂ part on one objective and the ♀ part on the other, as the original rows list them). The id must be in the avatarParts table (else rewardItemMissing).
quizDramasNote: Quiz quests (records of a quizTypes type with a before drama): the question was a board picture shown in that drama, and no original WW quiz drama survives. A quiz quest is served only when its quest key (events.json entries[].quests[].key, e.g. "EV-0484/+10") is listed here with the drama ids that show its board: {"<quest key>": {"ids": [drama ids], "reconstructed": true}} (a bare list of ids also works). The quiz boards task writes the list; until then every quiz quest is quizTextMissing. reconstructed true: label quizBoard (the board rebuilt from the khuxwiki text), or the entry's label: quizBoardFootage (redrawn from footage of the original), quizBoardScreenshot (a screenshot of the original). Part 4 Task 6: every quiz stage has its own drama and board (recon/tools/quiz_dramas.json, make_quiz_dramas.py writes them into the generated pack and the drama list stage_gen/event_dramas.json); the master run needs KHUX_EVENT_DRAMAS=D:/Progetto_Restauro_KH_UX/stage_gen/event_dramas.json, else these entries stop it.

reasonText.shared: This notice shares its quests with another row of the catalogue: they are built once, under the other row.
reasonText.board: In the original this event had no quests of its own: it was played on the event boards. Where its boards are served they are listed on this page; otherwise they come with a later update.
reasonText.coin: In the original this event had no quests of its own: it paid Event Coins for the event boards. Where its boards are served they are listed on this page; otherwise they come with a later update.
reasonText.undated: The original start date of this event is not known, so it cannot be placed in the calendar and is not listed.
reasonText.wikiEmpty: The khuxwiki page of this quest gives no map or no enemy we can identify, so it cannot be rebuilt yet.
reasonText.rewardItemMissing: A reward of this quest (a medal or a material) does not exist in our game data yet, so the quest is not served.
reasonText.notSelected: Not part of the events served so far.
reasonText.enemyMissing: An enemy of this quest is not in our game data yet (its model has to be found first), so the quest is not served: enemies are never replaced by another one.
reasonText.mapUnusable: The original map of this quest cannot be used yet (a file or a room is missing), so the quest is not served.
reasonText.mapKeyUsed: The map of this quest is already used by another quest of the events, so it cannot be built a second time.
reasonText.rewardRowsMissing: The reward rows of the enemies or chests on the map of this quest are not known yet, so the quest is not served.
reasonText.raidSpecial: This quest is a raid or Special stage, served by its own generator.
reasonText.worldMismatch: The original map of this quest lies in another world than the quest itself, so it is held back until it is checked.
reasonText.boosterOnly: Every reward of this quest is a Booster, and the Boosters do not exist on this server yet: the quest comes back with them, in a later update.
reasonText.rewardTypeUnknown: A reward of this quest is of a kind this server cannot give yet, so the quest is not served: it comes back when that reward can be given.
reasonText.quizTextMissing: This quiz quest asked its question on a picture board shown before the quest; that board is not in the surviving game files and has not been rebuilt yet, so the quest is not served.
reasonText.objectiveMismatch: The khuxwiki page and the surviving game data give different objectives for this quest, so it is held back until the right ones are confirmed.
reasonText.notice: An information notice of the original game, not an event: it had no quests of its own.
reasonText.objectiveUnmapped: An objective of this quest is known only from its text, and no surviving game data proves its code, so the quest is held back: it is never served with a guessed objective.
reasonText.scheduleLine: A second notice of an event that is listed under its own row: it had no quests of its own.
reasonText.enemyAmbiguous: This quest has no original map, and our game data holds several versions of one of its enemies with different strength: the quest is held back until the right version is confirmed, never guessed.
reasonText.avatarBoards: Avatar boards sold or handed out for a time, with no quest of their own: the boards served on this server are listed on this page with their price.
reasonText.hscNoQuest: No quest of this High Score Challenge survives in the game data we hold: it is not built yet.
reasonText.hscRewardUnmapped: A reward of this High Score Challenge could not be matched to an item of this server: it is not built yet.
reasonText.hscNoThresholds: The score thresholds that replace the original leaderboard of this High Score Challenge are not calibrated yet: it is not built yet.

reconstructedWhy.hscBaseRows: The khuxwiki page of this High Score Challenge names its enemies but not which version of each (our game data holds several, with different strength). The Japanese High Score maps of the same years place the base version for nearly all their enemies (2,204 of 2,424), so the base version of each name is used. Inferred, not original.
reconstructedWhy.hscJpTwin: The worldwide map file of this High Score Challenge is lost: it is in none of the game files or donated data we hold. The Japanese version ran a High Score Challenge with the same target, level and world on a map that survives; that map is used here. Layout reconstructed.
reconstructedWhy.mapPartSpare: Eight parts of this quest's map are missing from the surviving Japanese files. No path of the map leads into them (every enemy and chest of the quest is in the other parts), so they were filled with the map's own spare empty parts of the same room. The quest itself is played on the original map. Rebuilt, not original.
reconstructedWhy.damageContest: A Damage Contest («Test Your Might»): a High Score run whose score is the damage you deal to the target. Its rank brackets became score thresholds like those of the High Score Challenges (calibrated, not original). The July and October 2017 contests have no surviving map: they use the map of the December 2017 contest, the same quest (reconstructed).
reconstructedWhy.hscThresholds: In the original game the ranking rewards of a High Score Challenge went to the players by leaderboard position. This server has one player, so each original rank bracket became a score threshold: reach it with your best run and you receive that bracket's original rewards (only the highest bracket reached is paid; a better run later pays the difference, once per event). The thresholds are calibrated on the original scores where known, scaled from them or interpolated, as each one is marked. The rank shown is the best rank of the bracket you reached. The point milestones are the original ones.
reconstructedWhy.wikiRoom: No original map of this quest survives in any source we hold (the Japanese and worldwide game files, the donated data, the rooms rebuilt so far): its map was generated in the quest's original room (the room of its surviving stage data, else the room the khuxwiki page names), with the enemies and the target of the page at the quest's level. Not original.
reconstructedWhy.enemiesInferred: Some enemies of this quest could not be checked on the original footage (they were never hit, or fell to one special attack): their version was taken from the other quests of the same event, where it was measured. Inferred from the same run, not verified on footage.
reconstructedWhy.hpFromFootage: In the surviving game data the enemies «with little HP» of this event have 10 HP, which the original footage contradicts (they survive hits of several thousand). Their HP was estimated from the footage (the smallest value that fits the damage and the HP bar seen there) and scaled across levels like the normal version of the same enemy. HP estimated from footage, not original data.
reconstructedWhy.enemyRowRebuilt: One enemy of this quest (a Shadow shown with CAUTION in the original footage) is a version our game data lacked: no Shadow row we hold matches it. Its row was rebuilt from donated worldwide game data (its strength, Lux, attacks and countdown at every level), under a new id of its own because the donated id belongs to another enemy here, and it shows the Shadow model. The original footage confirms it (HP gauges and Lux per hit). Rebuilt from donated data, verified on footage.
reconstructedWhy.openWindowsReconstructed: In the original game this event's quests opened only for 12-hour periods, at times the notices never published. Here they open every day at the hours given in the Events notice (Pacific time), which are reconstructed, not original; outside them the event is not listed.
reconstructedWhy.openAllDay: In the original game this event's quests opened only for 12-hour periods, at times the notices never published. Here they stay open all day, every day of the event (not original).
reconstructedWhy.bonusHoursFactor: During this event's Bonus Time (the hours of the original notice, Pacific time) the Heartless drop rare Medals more often. The notice does not say by how much: here the drop rates are doubled in those hours (not original).
reconstructedWhy.bonusHoursLater: In the original game this event had a Bonus Time (hours of the original notice, Pacific time) when the Heartless dropped rare Medals more often. The drops of these quests are lost with their maps and are not rebuilt yet, so here there is nothing for the Bonus Time to raise.
reconstructedWhy.raidSummonLater: In the original game clearing this quest could make a raid boss appear (the notice or the khuxwiki page names it). No raid of that boss with the strength it had at that time is served yet, so here the quest summons no raid boss.
reconstructedWhy.dropsCalibrated: The drop rates of this quest are lost with its map. Its enemies drop what the event's notice named, at the rates of the original drop rows of a quest of the same kind (the KH 3D medal quests of 2017 or the event's own surviving maps). Reconstructed, not original.
reconstructedWhy.wikiAreas: The map of this quest spanned several areas (khuxwiki lists them, with the enemies and chests of each area). Its map file is lost, so the areas were rebuilt in that order, in the rooms of the quest's surviving stage data and of the khuxwiki pictures, joined by exits; start points, exits and enemy spots were taken from original maps of the same rooms where they survive, otherwise placed by the generator. The warp portals inside the areas (Xigbar's maze) are not rebuilt. Rebuilt, not original.
reconstructedWhy.jpReplayLayoutTwin: The worldwide map file of this quest is lost. The Japanese version replayed this very stage later on a map that survives (the same room and placement), with another target: that map is used with the worldwide target of this quest, read on the original footage. Layout reconstructed, enemy rows original.
reconstructedWhy.seriesLayoutTwin: The map file of this quest is lost. The same quest series ran again in another month on a map that survives (the same room, the same single enemy and target, every difficulty on the same map): that layout is used, with the enemy of this run, the original enemy row of these quests (its own strength at each difficulty). Layout reconstructed, enemy original.
reconstructedWhy.mapPartShared: One file of this quest's map (a part or its header) is missing from the surviving Japanese files, which kept only one copy of the map data the game shared between quests. It was taken from that shared copy, byte for byte: the map is the original one.
reconstructedWhy.mapHeaderRebuilt: The header of this quest's map (start point, target and the list of its parts) is missing from the surviving Japanese files, which kept only one copy of the data the game shared between quests. Five headers of the same event fit; they differ only in one running counter, so the first one was used. The map parts themselves are original. Rebuilt, not original.
reconstructedWhy.roomTilesRebuilt: The room of this quest's map lacks 4 picture tiles in the surviving Japanese files, which kept only one copy of the tiles the game shared. They lie in a band that is fully transparent in every other tile of the room and of its twin room, so they were rebuilt as transparent tiles. The map itself is original. Rebuilt, not original.
reconstructedWhy.mapPartRebuilt: One part of this quest's map (the empty lobby before the fight) is missing from the surviving Japanese files, which kept only one copy of the parts the game shared between quests. It was taken from another quest of the same event that starts the player at the same point in the same room; several nearly identical lobbies fit, and the nearest one was used. The fight itself is on the original map. Rebuilt, not original.
reconstructedWhy.jpTwinMap: The map of this quest is the Japanese map of the same quest, found by its content (the same enemies, counts, target and rooms at the quest's level): the worldwide map file of this run is lost.
reconstructedWhy.levelShifted: The map of this quest is a Japanese map with the same layout used at another level in the original; here its enemies fight at this quest's own level (khuxwiki), every enemy shifted by the same amount. The original map of this level is lost.
reconstructedWhy.unionTwin: In the original each Union had its own version of this quest; only one version survives in the game data. This Union's version was rebuilt from it (the same AP, level, restrictions and objectives, which khuxwiki gives identically for every Union) with the target of this Union's map file. You see only your own Union's version, and only it counts for the completion reward.
reconstructedWhy.donorKept: The quest keeps the values of the later game data; the khuxwiki page describes an earlier run of the same quest (2018), so it was not used for this one.
reconstructedWhy.wikiLowConfidence: One value of this quest comes from the khuxwiki page and could not be confirmed by a second source.
reconstructedWhy.mapIncomplete: The map file of this quest is incomplete in the data we have: the missing parts are reported, never invented.
reconstructedWhy.noWikiPage: No khuxwiki page exists for this quest: its values come from the later game data only, without a second source.
reconstructedWhy.wikiQuest: Quest rebuilt from the khuxwiki page: no master row of the original is known
reconstructedWhy.laterRun: The stage row and the map file of this quest are those of the same weekly quest in a later run (the row of this run is not in the data we have). Enemies, level, gem and rewards were checked against the khuxwiki page of this run; the AP, the gem and the world follow the page.
reconstructedWhy.wholeDay: In the original this event was open for a short window (minutes to hours); here it is open for its whole original day.
reconstructedWhy.communityBonus: In the original every player who cleared all the objectives of this event got a bonus sized by how many players did it worldwide (the official result notice gives the count). Here clearing every objective of its quests gives you, once, the bonus the original event reached, in your Presents: the count was of all players then, and is not redone for you alone (not original).
reconstructedWhy.completionReward: In the original every player who completed all the challenges of this event by the end of its campaign got this reward, the same for everyone (official notice). Here clearing every objective of its quests gives you the same reward, once, in your Presents.
reconstructedWhy.dramaOff: The original scenes before or after this quest are not shown yet.
reconstructedWhy.eventCoins: The Event Coin rewards of this event are paid into the balance of its event boards: one balance per board set, shared by the events of the set, and the coins never expire.
reconstructedWhy.boardsLater: The event boards of this event are not served yet: in the original every cell of a board paid a reward for its Event Coins, and every board of this set has a cell (or a board reward) that does not exist here yet, mostly a Booster. The boards come back whole in a later update, with the Boosters; until then its quests are served as a plain list, and the Event Coins they pay are kept in the balance of the set (they never expire) for when its boards are served.
reconstructedWhy.noCoinSource: The event boards of this event are not handed out yet: none of the quests that paid their Event Coins can be served yet, so the boards could not be filled.
reconstructedWhy.wikiAp: AP from the khuxwiki page of this run: the surviving game data (a later snapshot) gives another AP.
reconstructedWhy.wwEnemy: Map enemy changed to the WW enemy (khuxwiki): the Japanese map file of this quest places a different enemy than the worldwide quest had, so that one enemy was replaced by the worldwide one (same place, count, level and drops).
reconstructedWhy.boosterEffect: A reward of this quest is a Booster. Its effect is rebuilt from its original description (the original Booster data lost its effect values): which Medals or keyblade slots it strengthens and by how much are those of the description. It lasts as many days as in the original, counted from when you obtain it.
reconstructedWhy.boosterExpiryWindow: No surviving notice gives the expiry of this Booster: it lasts until the end of the original event that paid it, counted in days from when you obtain it.
reconstructedWhy.boardArt: A card picture of this event's boards is not in any game data we hold: it is the picture of the original card cut from a screenshot of the original board (or taken from the community wiki), not the original file.
reconstructedWhy.boosterIdByName: The original board names this Booster but not which of its identical copies it paid: each cell pays a different copy, so they add up as in the original.
reconstructedWhy.boosterLater: A reward of this quest was a Booster, which does not exist on this server yet: it is recorded for you when you complete its objective, and given when the Boosters come (a later update). The other rewards are paid as usual.
reconstructedWhy.noBoardSet: This event paid Event Coins, but no source names the board set they were for: its Event Coins are not paid here (they are only logged) until its boards are identified.
reconstructedWhy.quizBoard: The original question board of this quiz is not in the surviving game files: it was redrawn in the original style from the question text recorded on khuxwiki.
reconstructedWhy.quizBoardFootage: The original question board of this quiz is not in the surviving game files: it was redrawn from footage of the original game, with the same text and layout.
reconstructedWhy.quizBoardScreenshot: The original question board of this quiz is not in the surviving game files: it comes from a screenshot of the original game (khuxwiki), scaled to the game screen, with the SKIP button of the screenshot removed.

mapRestoreNote: make-events.js mapRestoreLabels (Events Part 5, user decision 6, 10-11-2026): an imported map with a part or STG filled from its JP dedup-stub source (recon/tools/import_event_stages.py report partSources) gets mapPartShared when the copy is exact (reconstructed false), else the label of partSourceLabels[basis] (default mapPartRebuilt); a map on a room of rebuiltRooms gets that room's label (the room build completed it: recon/tools/make_jp_rooms.py DEDUP_TILES).
